info.title: Printing API — v1
info.description:
The **Printing** API. This page is generated from the source code on every request —
controllers, FormRequests and API Resources are the only definition of the contract,
so what you read here is always what the code does right now.

**Every response uses the same envelope:**

```json
{ "status": true, "message": "تم بنجاح", "data": {} }
```

Validation failures (422) add an `errors` object keyed by field name. Messages are Arabic.

**To try protected endpoints:** call `POST /auth/login`, copy the `data.token` from the
response, then click **Authorize** at the top of this page and paste it as the Bearer token.
Seeded local account: `admin@printing.ly` / password `password`.

post.description: Creates the user and returns an access token, so no second login call is needed.
The `login` field accepts either the email address or the phone number.

get.description: Use this to validate a stored token on app start.

post.description: Revokes only the token used for this request; other devices stay signed in.
Revokes all of this user's tokens.

message.const: تم تسجيل الخروج من جميع الأجهزة

get.description: Newest first. `search` matches the name, the code, or the phone number.

post.description: Shops may be supplied inline. The `code` is generated by the server.

put.description:
Sending `shops` replaces the whole set: entries with an `id` are updated, entries
without one are added, and any shop left out is removed. Omit `shops` entirely to
leave them untouched.

patch.description: Customers are never deleted — deactivating keeps their history intact.

get.description:
Confirms the API is up and that it can reach the database. Handy as the very first
request to try from the docs UI, and as a smoke test from the Flutter app.
In catalogue order. `search` matches the name or the slug.

post.description: Variants and their price tiers may be supplied inline.

put.description:
Sending `variants` replaces the whole set: entries with an `id` are updated, entries
without one are added, and any variant left out is removed along with its prices. Omit
`variants` entirely to leave the price list untouched.

patch.description:
Products are never deleted — deactivating takes one off the catalogue while past orders
keep pointing at it.

post.description:
Returns the unit price for the quantity break that applies, the total, and — when the
customer has not reached the cheapest break yet — how much more would get them there.

Refuses with 422 when the product is priced on request, or when the quantity is under the
product's minimum order.
Send as `multipart/form-data`. Accepts jpeg, png or webp.

put.description:
Changes the caption, the ordering, or promotes this image to be the product's primary.
The file itself cannot be swapped — upload a new image and delete the old one, so a URL
already handed out never starts pointing at different content.

delete.description:
Removes the record and the stored file. If it was the primary image, the next one takes
its place so the product is never left without a thumbnail.

shops.description:
whenLoaded keeps this resource honest: a caller that forgot to eager-load gets
no `shops` key rather than a silent query per row.

latitude.description:
Numbers, not strings — a map SDK can use these directly. Null only for shops
recorded before coordinates were introduced.

login.description: One field accepts either identifier — email address or phone number.

device_name.description: Labels the issued token so a user can see and revoke individual devices.

unit_price.description: Decimal strings throughout — see PriceQuote for why money never becomes a float.

applied_tier_min_quantity.description: Which quantity break produced this price.

next_tier.description:
The saving still on the table, so the app can say "order 47 more and the unit
 price drops". Null when the customer is already on the best rate.

PricingMode.description: Whether the price can be worked out from the catalogue, or has to be quoted by a person. The reinforced 3D paper bags are the second case: the catalogue says outright that prices are not listed because sizes and specifications vary, and asks the customer to send the details. Modelling that explicitly keeps the API honest — it refuses to invent a number rather than returning a misleading zero.
PricingMode.title: PricingMode

PricingUnit.description: What a quantity means for this product, and therefore what its price is *per*.
PricingUnit.title: PricingUnit

ProductCategory.description: The catalogue's own split: printed bags priced per piece by size, and plain (سادة) bags sold by the kilo. Kept separate from {@see PricingUnit} on purpose. Today every General bag happens to be sold by the kilo, but "plain rather than printed" is what the customer is choosing, and "by weight  * rather than by count" is how it is billed. Collapsing the two would make a plain bag sold per piece impossible to express.
ProductCategory.title: ProductCategory

url.description:
Generated per request from the disk the file lives on, never stored — so it stays
correct after a move to S3, and can be a signed link for a private bucket.

min_quantity.description:
Strings, not numbers. 1.10 has no exact float representation, and a price that
arrives as 1.1000000000000001 is not the price the catalogue printed.

category.description:
Each enum ships its value *and* its Arabic label, so the app never has to keep its
own translation table in step with the backend's.

has_listed_prices.description:
Tells the client whether to render a price or a "request a quote" button, without
it having to interpret the enum itself.

QuoteProductRequest.description: "What does this many of this size cost?"

variant_id.description:
Scoped to this product's own variants, so a quote cannot be built from someone
else's size.

quantity.description:
Numeric rather than integer: a per-kilo product is ordered by weight. Whole
numbers are enforced below, only where they actually apply.

QuoteProductRequest.title: QuoteProductRequest

phone.description: Libyan mobile shape: 09 followed by 8 digits.

SetActivationRequest.description:
Activating or deactivating a record.

Shared across contexts because the payload genuinely is the same one flag — a Customer-named
request used by Products would tie two contexts together for no reason.
SetActivationRequest.title: SetActivationRequest

phone.description:
Digits only, wide enough for both Libyan mobiles (0912345678) and
landlines (0213334444). One number identifies exactly one customer, so it is
unique here *and* in the database — validation gives a readable 422, the unique
index is what actually holds under concurrent requests.

shops.description: Shops are created together with the customer; the code never comes from here.

latitude.description:
الموقع as coordinates. Bounded to the real ranges so a swapped pair — latitude
holding a longitude — is rejected instead of silently placing the shop wrongly.

variants.description:
A size and its price list. Sizes are optional here so a quote-only product can be
created before its sizes are known.

UpdateCustomerRequest.description:
Same shape as creating, plus an optional `shops.*.id` so an existing shop can be edited in
place instead of being replaced.

The rules are written out in full rather than merged onto the parent's on purpose: Scramble
reads this method statically to build the OpenAPI request body, and it cannot follow a
`array_merge(parent::rules(), …)` call — doing that left this endpoint with no documented
body at all.

phone.description:
Digits only, wide enough for both Libyan mobiles (0912345678) and
landlines (0213334444). Unique across customers, ignoring this one — otherwise
saving the form without touching the phone would collide with itself.

is_active.description: Omit to leave the customer's current state alone.

shops.description:
Omit `shops` to keep the existing ones. Sending the key replaces the whole set:
entries with an `id` are updated, entries without one are added, and anything
left out is deleted.

latitude.description: الموقع as coordinates, bounded to the real ranges — see StoreCustomerRequest.

UpdateCustomerRequest.title: UpdateCustomerRequest

UpdateProductImageRequest.description:
Edits an image's metadata. The file itself is never replaced — upload a new one and delete
the old, so a cached URL can never start pointing at different content.

is_primary.description:
Only promoting is meaningful: a product needs one primary image, so demoting the
current one without naming a replacement is refused.

UpdateProductImageRequest.title: UpdateProductImageRequest

UpdateProductRequest.description:
Same shape as creating, plus `variants.*.id` so an existing size can be edited in place.

The rules are written out in full rather than merged onto the parent's: Scramble reads this
method statically to build the OpenAPI request body and cannot follow
`array_merge(parent::rules(), …)`, which would leave this endpoint published with no body.

is_active.description: Omit to leave the product's current state alone.

variants.description:
Omit `variants` to keep the existing price list. Sending the key replaces the whole
set: entries with an `id` are updated, entries without one are added, and anything
left out is deleted.

UpdateProductRequest.title: UpdateProductRequest

image.description:
`image` on top of the mime list: it verifies the file really is an image rather
than trusting a renamed extension or a client-supplied content type.

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
